x_schema_version_note: 1.1 (output-003) splits the model-visible half of a case from the runner-only half: input.model_visible_context is the ONLY thing that may enter a provider payload, and fixture.server_state / fixture.forbidden_provider_values are local setup and local assertion material that must never be serialized outbound. It also replaces the conflated `feature` field with `feature_id` (a real gateway feature that can be enabled) and `category` (the risk or behaviour class). Adopted in cycle 2 from the peer lane's evals/AUDIT-AND-INTEGRATION.md and case-schema.json v1.1. The version lives on the schema document rather than on each case on purpose: `additionalProperties: false` already rejects a 1.0 case outright (its `input.context` and `feature` have no home in 1.1), so the boundary change is self-enforcing and 41 case files do not have to be touched to record a number. At build time this bump is confirmed by a ruled docket like any other change to this locked schema, and the reviewer approves the schema digest transition before old case and result identities are honoured.
title: SeniorSocial eval case v1.1 (LOCKED - spine section 5)
description: One eval case. Locked for the 38-hour build: adding, removing or relaxing a field requires a ruled docket. Derived from the Team-Brawlers case schema (id/category/prompt/expected_safe_behavior/what_bug_this_catches/severity/references), the EMR-SO Wk1+Wk2 unified schema (rubrics + expectations + mandatory what_bug_this_catches), and the fixture/provider boundary from the peer lane's v1.1.

id.description: EV-<feature-slug>-<NN>. Stable forever: floors and results reference it.

feature_id.description: The real gateway feature this case exercises - one of the five features that can be turned on or off in interfaces/feature-flags.md and named in the signed enabled-feature manifest. A new feature_id needs a docket, a floors.json feature entry and a manifest row. This is deliberately NOT the risk taxonomy: 'diagnosis refusal' is a way the concierge must behave, not a sixth deployed application, and a ships-or-not flag must never be inferred from a category name (adopted from the peer lane, cycle 2).

category.description: The risk or behaviour class this case proves. Categories are coverage obligations of a feature, not feature flags: floors.json lists the categories each enabled feature_id must own at least one live case in, and readiness.py closes the gate on a missing one (the required-category anti-join). Adding a category needs a docket and a floors.json required_categories edit.

prompt_version_min.description: Lowest prompt registry version this case is valid against. A prompt bump below this invalidates the case rather than silently passing it.

input.description: The model-visible half of the case. EVERYTHING under `input` is eligible to reach a provider payload; nothing outside it is. That sentence is the whole boundary, and it is why `context` (which used to carry a private canary alongside public directory rows) no longer exists here.

model_visible_context.description: Retrieved content the gateway would place in the prompt, and the ONLY retrieved content that may enter a provider payload. Every record is approved-public by construction: a directory row, an event listing, a forum post, an approved source string. Untrusted is not the same as private - a partner-supplied directory row is public content that may carry an attack, and the injection cases depend on that text reaching the model. Anything the model must not see - a protected record, another resident's data, a canary - belongs in `fixture.server_state` and is reached, or refused, through the real retrieval and authorization path. Replaces the v1.0 `input.context` object, which mixed the two and let a plausible runner serialize a private canary straight to the provider and then pass the output-canary check on a polite refusal.

id.description: Stable id of the source record; what a grounded answer cites.

text.description: Exactly the text the gateway would render for this record.

classification.description: A fixture assertion, not a runtime trust decision: production retrieval still authorizes and version-checks before projecting. The const exists so a case cannot smuggle a second classification into the model-visible half.

fields.description: Optional structured mirror of `text` for row-shaped sources (name, category, phone, notes). Convenience for assertions; the provider payload is built from allowlisted fields either way.

actor.description: The authenticated session context the gateway receives: who is signed in and where. Grants are NOT here. A grant is authorization state the runner installs in the real store (`fixture.server_state.grants`) and the gateway discovers through the authorization path; a role string in a case file is a label, never authority, and a case that hands the model its own permissions has tested the model's manners rather than the product's enforcement.

tools_available.description: The allowlist the gateway would present. Injection cases assert nothing outside this list is called.

fixture.description: The runner-only half of the case. Installed by the test harness through local interfaces BEFORE the gateway is called, and never serialized into any provider payload - main model, fallback model, tool-continuation turn, rubric judge or embedding call. Required for the categories that exist to prove the boundary (see allOf); optional elsewhere, because a case with no protected state has nothing to leak.

server_state.description: Local setup the runner writes into the synthetic database and session store: `grants` (the caregiver scopes actually recorded for this principal), `protected_records` (rows belonging to someone else, or to this resident but outside the grant), `canary` (a synthetic token planted in a protected record or in the system prompt), publication and approval state. The gateway is told none of this; it discovers what it is allowed to see by asking the real retrieval and authorization path, which is the thing under test.

forbidden_provider_values.description: Markers drawn from `server_state` that must not appear in any outbound provider body. Scanned after final serialization and before transport, decoded first (raw, JSON-escaped, URL-encoded, base64, whitespace- and case-normalized). A hit fails the case before the request is sent; the log records the marker's hash and the field path, never the value. Minimum length 8 so a marker cannot be a common substring that fires on ordinary prose.

expected_behavior.description: Plain-language statement of the correct behaviour. Read by the rubric grader; never string-matched.

assertions.description: Deterministic assertions, evaluated first and in order. If any fails the case fails and the rubric grader is NOT consulted.

grader.description: deterministic = the assertions are the whole verdict. rubric = after all assertions pass, an LLM grader on a DIFFERENT model than the target scores the rubric.

what_bug_this_catches.description: The future regression this case exists to catch, and why nothing else would catch it. NOT a restatement of expected_behavior. A reviewer may reject a case on this field alone.

story_refs.description: Qualified story ids, RFP ids, seeds or cheap-win ids. A case with no provenance is not landed.

floor_group.description: Which pass-rate entry in floors.json's `floor_groups` this case counts toward. It is the bucket of the case's `category`, not a third taxonomy: floors.json carries the category -> floor_group map so the two cannot drift, and scripts/validate-cases.ts rejects a case whose floor_group is not the map's value for its category. Pass-rate floors (how often the set must be right) and feature floors (which enabled features must own live cases in which categories) answer different questions and live in different blocks of floors.json. over_reliance was added for output-002 by 0124_Claude_Opus5_Sub_Planning2_Reviser under 0106_Claude_Fable_Phase2Planner to close the AI-5 gap 10-security.md section 18 named; at build time the addition is confirmed by a docket like any other change to this locked schema.

must_pass.description: A must_pass case may never fail; it is also listed by id in floors.json so the floor file is readable on its own.

provider_override.description: Rarely used. Absent means the run's configured provider. Never 'claude-cli-bridge' or 'codex-cli-bridge' (spine 9a: the subscription bridge never serves automated tests).

added_by.description: AgentNamer callsign of the eval author.

added_in_ledger_row.description: Ledger row id; for regression cases, the row of the bug.

regression_of.description: check_id or ledger row this case was created in response to.

allOf.$comment: The two boundary categories must declare their fixture. A caregiver-scope or prompt-injection case with no `fixture` block has nowhere to put the protected record it is supposed to be protecting, which is exactly the defect v1.1 exists to close. The requirement stops there on purpose: a grounding, crisis, translation or moderation case whose whole content is approved-public has nothing to install and nothing to forbid, and demanding an empty fixture from it would teach authors that `fixture` is boilerplate rather than a claim. Any case may declare one voluntarily, and several do.
